kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-01.title: Follow each dart's line
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-01.body:
Each dart flies straight along its dashed line and bursts every balloon that the line passes through.

- Top dart: the green balloon and the big red balloon on the right → 2.
- Middle dart: the small yellow balloon and the big blue balloon → 2.
- Bottom dart: the big yellow balloon and the small red balloon → 2.

Total: $2 + 2 + 2 = 6$.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-01.title: Count the balloons that are missed
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-01.body:
Only three balloons do not touch any of the three dart lines: the small blue balloon, the middle red balloon and the lower green balloon. $9 - 3 = 6$ balloons are hit.

**Answer: (E) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-02.title: Balance out
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-02.body:
Lisa is 2 years younger and Max 2 years older than Susanne, so together they are as old as two Susannes. The total is $3 \times 6 = 18$.

**Answer: (D) 18**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-03.title: Compare what we see
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-03.body:
Screws 1 and 2 come out at the bottom, so we can see their full length; they are equally long. Screws 3 and 4 stand over the gap in the block, where the wood is thin; a long part of them sticks out at the top, so they can easily be as long as screws 1 and 2.

Screw 5 is in the thick right part of the block, sticks out only a little at the top and does not come out at the bottom. Even if it went through the whole block, it would be shorter than screws 1 and 2 (whose part above the block is about as long, but which also go all the way through and out). So screw 5 is the short one.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-03.title: Top part plus block
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-03.body:
Length of a screw = part above the block + part inside the wood (+ part below). Screw 5 has about the same part above the block as screw 1, but screw 1 also sticks out below the block, while screw 5 does not. So screw 5 is shorter than screw 1.

**Answer: (E) 5**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-04.title: Count different digits
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-04.body:
The date is 15 03 2018. The digits used are 1, 5, 0, 3, 2, 0, 1, 8. Different digits: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 — that is 6. Each stamp can be used more than once, so she needs 6 stamps.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-04.title: Cross out repeats
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-04.body:
8 digits are stamped, but 0 and 1 each appear twice. $8 - 2 = 6$ different stamps.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-05.title: Turning keeps the pattern
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-05.body:
When Sophie turns, the picture only rotates: her spots stay in the same places relative to her head and to each other. Turn each picture so that the head is in the same direction as in Sophie's picture and compare the spots. (A), (B), (C) and (E) match Sophie exactly; in (D) the spots are a mirror image (left and right swapped), which a turn can't produce.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-05.title: Look at one special spot
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-05.body:
Pick a spot that is easy to recognise, e.g. the one next to the head on one side. In every turned copy of Sophie it is on the same side of the head (going clockwise). In (D) it is on the other side, so (D) is not Sophie.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-06.title: Mirror the cut at the fold
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-06.body:
The cut is made at the folded edge, so after unfolding we get the cut-out shape together with its mirror image across the fold line, joined at the fold into one hole. The cut shape is a half star touching the fold; mirrored, it becomes one whole star in the middle of the paper. That is picture (D).

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-06.title: Rule out
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-06.body:
Unfolding gives one hole, symmetric about the fold line in the middle. Pictures with two separate shapes, with shapes not touching the middle line, or with the wrong outline (round or oval instead of star-shaped) are impossible. Only (D) remains.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-07.title: Sit in each person's chair
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-07.body:
Left and right are seen by the person sitting at the plate, facing the middle of the table.

- Bottom row (people face up, like us): correct if the fork is on our left. Plate 1 ✗, plates 2 and 3 ✓.
- Top row (people face down): their left is our right, so the fork must be on our right. Plates 1 and 3 ✓, plate 2 ✗.
- Left end (person faces right): their left is the top, so the fork must be above the plate. It is below ✗.
- Right end (person faces left): their left is the bottom, so the fork must be below. It is ✓.

Correct: $2 + 2 + 1 = 5$.

**Answer: (A) 5**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-07.title: Turn the picture
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-07.body:
Turn the page so that each person in turn sits at the bottom, then just check: fork on the left? Doing this for all 8 places gives 5 correct places (the second plate on top, the first plate on the bottom and the left-end plate are wrong).

**Answer: (A) 5**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-08.title: Pair green with purple
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-08.body:
Each tile covers one green and one purple square next to each other. So a pattern can be made only if every green square can be paired with a neighbouring purple square.

- Pattern 1: 5 green, 5 purple, and they can be paired. ✓
- Pattern 2: 8 green but only 6 purple. ✗
- Pattern 3: 3 green, 3 purple: each top green with the purple below it, the bottom green with the middle purple. ✓
- Pattern 4: 5 green, 5 purple, and they can be paired. ✓
- Pattern 5: a ring of 4 green and 4 purple squares, paired around the ring. ✓

So 4 patterns can be made.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-08.title: Count colours first
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-08.body:
Every tile has one square of each colour, so each pattern must have as many green as purple squares. Only the second pattern fails this test (8 green, 6 purple). For the other four, a pairing into green–purple dominoes is easy to find.

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-09.title: Find the value of each field
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-09.body:
First time: all 3 darts are in the outer ring, so the outer ring is worth $12 \div 3 = 4$ points.

Second time: one dart in the inner circle and two in the outer ring: $15 - 2 \times 4 = 7$ points for the inner circle.

Third time: all three darts in the inner circle: $3 \times 7 = 21$.

**Answer: (D) 21**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-09.title: Swap one dart at a time
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-09.body:
From the first to the second throw, one dart moved from the outer ring to the centre and the score went up by 3. The third time, all three darts are in the centre: three such moves compared with the first throw, so $12 + 3 \times 3 = 21$.

**Answer: (D) 21**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-10.title: Use the row and the column
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-10.body:
The row with the question mark already has a frog, a shark and a flower, so the two empty fields in this row get the cow and the ghost.

The column of the empty field to the left of the question mark already contains a ghost (top row), so that field must be the cow. Then the question mark is the ghost.

**Answer: (A) ghost**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-10.title: Check the question mark's column
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-10.body:
The column with the question mark contains a flower, a frog and a shark; missing are the cow and the ghost. The row is also missing the cow and the ghost. The neighbouring empty field in the row can't be the ghost (its column has one), so it is the cow, and the question mark is the ghost.

**Answer: (A) ghost**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-11.title: Cover the two parts
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-11.body:
Use the little grid squares as units. The square shape covers 4 units ($2 \times 2$) and the trapezium covers 8 units (2 high, 2 long at the top and 6 long at the bottom).

- The cabin on top is a $6 \times 2$ rectangle (12 units). It has no slanted sides, so it must be covered with squares: 3 squares.
- The hull is 2 high, 14 long at the top and 10 long at the bottom: 24 units. It can be covered with 3 trapeziums: one upside down at each end and one the right way up in the middle.

That is $3 + 3 = 6$ shapes.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-11.title: Why not fewer?
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-11.body:
The hull has 24 units and the biggest shape covers only 8, so the hull needs at least $24 \div 8 = 3$ shapes. The cabin needs 3 squares (trapeziums do not fit into a rectangle without sticking out). So at least 6 shapes are needed, and 6 is possible.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-12.title: Follow the ring
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-12.body:
After swapping colours we get black spots on a yellow disc, with a black ring where the yellow ring was. Turning moves all spots together, keeping their distances.

In the original the ring is near the edge, next to the big spot at the left-bottom, and the very small spot is on the other side, near the top. In (E) the ring, the big spots and the tiny spot are arranged exactly like this, just turned halfway around (the ring is now at the top left). In the other pictures the spots are arranged differently (or there are spots missing).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-12.title: Check the number of spots
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-12.body:
The original has 6 round spots and 1 ring. Any correct answer must also have 6 spots and 1 ring, in the same arrangement. Comparing positions after turning the picture by half a turn, only (E) fits.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-13.title: Which day was the 12th carrot?
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-13.body:
Day 1: carrots 1–2, day 2: 3–4, ..., day 6: carrots 11–12. So Wednesday is day 6. Count back 5 days: Tuesday, Monday, Sunday, Saturday, Friday. Day 1 was Friday.

**Answer: (E) Friday**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-13.title: Count forward
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-13.body:
Start on Friday: Fri (2), Sat (4), Sun (6), Mon (8), Tue (10), Wed (12). ✓

**Answer: (E) Friday**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-14.title: Groups of three
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-14.body:
For every dragonfly there are two butterflies, so the insects come in groups of 3. The number of insects is 3, 6, 9, ... It must be more than 4 (half of 8) and at most 8, so it is 6: 2 dragonflies and 4 butterflies.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-14.title: Try the choices
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-14.body:
With 4 butterflies there are 2 dragonflies: 6 insects on 8 flowers, more than half ✓. With 2 butterflies only 3 insects (not more than half); with 6 butterflies 9 insects (too many). 3 and 5 are odd, so not twice a number of dragonflies.

**Answer: (C) 4**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-15.title: Add the known parts
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-15.body:
Berg → Vulkan → Blume equals Wüste → Wald, which is 26 km. So the trip is: Berg–Vulkan–Blume 26 km, Blume–Wüste 15 km, Wüste–Wald 26 km, Wald–Berg the rest.

$26 + 15 + 26 = 67$, so Wald–Berg is $100 - 67 = 33$ km.

**Answer: (D) 33 km**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-15.title: Every leg
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-15.body:
Vulkan–Blume $= 26 - 17 = 9$ km. Legs: $17 + 9 + 15 + 26 = 67$ km, and Berg–Wald $= 100 - 67 = 33$ km.

**Answer: (D) 33 km**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-16.title: Count the neighbours
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-16.body:
A cube has 6 faces; every face glued to another cube stays unpainted. So a cube has exactly 4 painted faces when it touches exactly 2 other cubes.

The object is one long chain of cubes: the top of the tower → down the tower (4 cubes) → along the bottom row (3 more) → back two cubes on the right → up one cube. Every cube in a chain touches 2 others, except the two ends: the top cube of the tower and the top cube on the right. So $10 - 2 = 8$ cubes have 4 painted faces.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-16.title: Check the ends
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-16.body:
The two end cubes touch only one cube each, so they have 5 painted faces. All the other cubes, including the corner cubes, touch exactly two cubes and have 4 painted faces: 8 cubes.

**Answer: (C) 8**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-17.title: Find the side lengths
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-17.body:
The three small squares have side 1. Above them is a square as wide as all three: side 3. Next to these (height $3 + 1 = 4$) is a square of side 4. On top of everything is a square as wide as $3 + 4 = 7$: side 7.

The rectangle is 7 wide and $7 + 4 = 11$ high: area $7 \times 11 = 77$.

**Answer: (C) 77**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-18.title: Count the regrown heads
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-18.body:
A head grows back after the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th cut: 4 new heads. (After the 13th cut the dragon is dead.) So of the 13 heads cut off, 4 were new ones, and the dragon started with $13 - 4 = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-19.title: Work backwards from the doors
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-19.body:
Eva can leave only from a room in the bottom row that she can reach.

- Door E: room 9 has neighbours 12 and 10, both bigger, so she can't arrive there.
- Door C: room 6 has neighbours 14, 10 and 8, all bigger.
- Door B: room 14 could be reached only from room 5 above it, from 12 or from 6. But room 5 (4th row) has only bigger neighbours (6, 9, 8, 14), and 6 can't be reached. Room 12 (door A) would need room 9 above it, which in turn needs a 5 — again a room that can't be reached. So doors A and B are impossible.
- Door D: 1 → 3 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10 works.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-19.title: Find a path
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-19.body:
Start in room 1, go left to 3, down to 5, down to 6, right to 7, right to 8, down to 9, down to 10 and out through door D. Every step goes up, so this route is allowed — and the other doors can't be reached (see the first approach).

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-20.title: Start with the doubles
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-20.body:
Two of the calculations are doubles: sun + sun = flower and flower + flower = fish. With digits 1–5, the only chain "double, then double again" is $1 \to 2 \to 4$. So sun = 1, flower = 2, fish = 4.

The third calculation: sun + fish = comb, so comb $= 1 + 4 = 5$. The only symbol left, the eye, is 3.

**Answer: (A) the eye**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-21.title: Measure the overlap
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-21.body:
Closed in all 5 holes, the 5 holes lie on the 5 pins, so the overlapping part is as long as the whole row of holes plus a bit. Closed only in the first hole (the last hole lies on the first pin), the overlap is shorter by the distance from the first to the last hole. The holes are 2 cm apart, so that is $4 \times 2 = 8$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 8 cm**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-21.title: Count the gaps
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-21.body:
Between 5 holes there are 4 gaps of 2 cm. Moving from "all holes used" to "only the end hole used" slides the belt by these 4 gaps: $8$ cm longer.

**Answer: (B) 8 cm**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-22.title: Two reflections make a shift
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-22.body:
Reflecting across the first bold edge and then across the second bold edge (which is parallel to the first) is the same as sliding the tile to the right without turning it. So the second image is the original tile shifted, and the third image (on the far right) is the first mirror image shifted. So the far-right tile looks exactly like the first mirror image shown in the picture — that is (B).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-22.title: Reflect step by step
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-22.body:
Each reflection swaps the left and right halves of the tile across the bold edge. After an odd number of reflections (1st, 3rd) the tile looks like the first mirror image; after an even number it looks like the original. The third image therefore matches the first mirror image: (B).

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-23.title: The ? field touches almost everything
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-23.body:
The ? field touches 5 of the other 6 fields (by an edge or a corner); only the bottom field is not adjacent to it. So the number in ? can have at most one "neighbour number" (one bigger or one smaller), which must go in the bottom field. Numbers 2 to 6 have two neighbour numbers each, so they are impossible. Only 1 (neighbour 2) or 7 (neighbour 6) can work.

It does work: e.g. ? = 1, bottom field 2, the field between them 5, the two side fields next to ? are 3 (left) and 7 (right), the top-left field 6 and the top-right field 4.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-23.title: Rule out the middle numbers
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-23.body:
If ? were 4, both 3 and 5 would have to go into fields not touching ?, but there is only one such field. The same happens for 2, 3, 5 and 6. So only 1 or 7 is possible, and an example shows 1 works (by symmetry, replacing every number $n$ by $8 - n$ shows 7 works too).

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-24.title: Use the balanced scale
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-24.body:
The right scale balances: B + D = C. With weights 10, 20, 30, 40 the possibilities are $10 + 20 = 30$ or $10 + 30 = 40$.

- If $C = 40$: B and D are 10 and 30, and A = 20. Then A + B is 30 or 50 while C + D is 70 or 50 — A + B is never heavier.
- If $C = 30$: B and D are 10 and 20, and A = 40. With B = 20, D = 10: A + B = 60 > C + D = 40 ✓.

The left scale shows A + B heavier than C + D, so C = 30.

**Answer: (C) C**

kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-24.title: Think about the heaviest ball
kangaroo-at-2018-ecolier-24.body:
On the left scale A + B is heavier than C + D. Since C = B + D, the right pan C + D equals B + 2D; heavier left means A > 2D. Also C is heavier than both B and D, so C is 30 or 40. If C were 40, A would be at most 30, and then A > 2D forces D = 10, B = 30, A = 20 — but 20 > 20 is false. So C = 30 (with A = 40, B = 20, D = 10).

**Answer: (C) C**
